precepts.text: Later in history king Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly; the same pattern seen with Micah's mother.
precepts.point: A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel; there were mothers who steered a son down the wrong path.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

precepts.why:
Micah’s mother, instead of rebuking a son who stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from her, said “Blessed be thou of the Lord, my son”, and had a graven image and a molten image made to set up in his house. A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel. Later in history king Ahaziah “walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.”

It is the same pattern. There were mothers in Israel who steered a son down the wrong path, and Micah’s mother was one of them, counselling her son into idolatry with the very silver he had stolen from her.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why:
“For his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.” Some of you brothers listening, it’s either your mama or your wife is your counselor, or your big sister: you are not a man. In New York a brother said sister such-and-such is my counselor; you better get the hell up on out of here.

We have seen in IUIC mothers counseling their sons in wickedness. Where’d you get that from, brother? My mama. You sisters that married his mama’s boy, shame on you: marrying him is like marrying his mama, mama calling you on the phone and paying you a visit. Who wants to live like that?

moments.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. That is the same thing that mother was explaining with her daughters and her sons. Sons got to do whatever and be whatever. And they did not have any real guidance, because the mother did not know how. But she was raising her daughters to be so-called better than her, tough and independent. And she noticed that she was creating a bigger problem, because now they have got a mindset that they do not need a man.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Daughters need men too. Because nowhere in the Bible have you seen a successful woman on her own. She went from her father to a husband. And if she did not have a husband she was always under the guidance of the elder men.

Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellers after the death of his father to his destruction. And that is where we are at with society. We have taught our kids that they are nothing.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his stead, for the band of Arabians had slain all the elder sons.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign and reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.

This is a warning against being ruled by the wrong counsel: instead of going to the priests and the judges, he went to his mother, and she counselled him into ruin. A woman with a grudge can rule a kingdom through her son, and that is what Athaliah did.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father died, to his destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: Ahaziah walked after their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram was wounded.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: He went down to see the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel, and the destruction of Ahaziah was of the Most High, for by going he came into the path of Jehu, whom the Most High had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: That same Jehu who killed the seventy sons of Ahab found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brethren and slew them, then sought and caught Ahaziah, who was hid in Samaria.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: They buried Ahaziah for the sake of Jehoshaphat his forefather who sought the Most High with all his heart; but the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom, so the wicked king was cut off by the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah, killing the king's sons.
Athaliah did not carry out this slaughter alone; she had weak men helping her run over everything, which is how she seized and held the throne.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: But Jehoshabeath the daughter of king Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, hiding him and his nurse in a bedchamber.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: She hid the child in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned over the land, showing that Athaliah was ruling in the position of the son she had lost.
